Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes and challenges that come with becoming a new mother. It's completely normal to feel overwhelmed, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand your emotional well-being during this postpartum period. The EPDS is a tool that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us have a more informed discussion about your mental health.

Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. My goal is to provide you with a non-judgmental and empathetic ear, and to work together to identify any areas where you might need additional support.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your emotions and experiences over the past week. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and comfortable as possible.

So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. (sigh) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still laugh and smile when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same as before. I feel like I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to make me happy. Even when my friends or family try to make me laugh, it's just not as easy for me to find the humor in things like it was before I had the baby. Some days are better than others, but overall, I'd say I've been feeling pretty down and it's hard for me to see the funny side of things like I used to. (pausing, looking down) It's like, I know I should be happy and enjoying this time with my new baby, but it's just not feeling that way for me right now.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(pausing, reflecting) Yeah, I guess that's true. I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, but it's just not as often as I'd like. Like, the other day, my baby spit up all over my favorite shirt, and my husband and I both just burst out laughing. It was one of those moments where you just have to laugh, you know? But, to be honest, those moments are kind of few and far between for me right now. Most of the time, I'm just feeling really overwhelmed and worried about everything. (sighing) I don't know, it's just hard for me to find the joy in things like I used to. Even when I do laugh, it's not always genuine, you know? Sometimes I'm just laughing to try to make everyone else feel better, but deep down, I'm still feeling really sad and anxious. (looking down, fidgeting) Does that make sense?
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really... I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but lately, it's just been so hard to muster up any excitement. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting up with friends, just feel like so much work now. I know I should be looking forward to these things, but honestly, most of the time I'm just feeling really tired and overwhelmed. (sighing) And it's not just that I'm not looking forward to things, it's that I'm also worried about how they'll go. Like, will the baby cry the whole time? Will I be able to get everything ready on time? It's just so much anxiety and stress, and it's hard for me to enjoy anything when I'm feeling like that. (pausing, looking down) I feel like I've just lost my sense of joy and anticipation, and it's really hard for me to imagine feeling that way again. (starting to tear up) Sorry... it's just really hard for me to talk about this stuff.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, looking down) Oh, yeah... I do that all the time. I feel like I'm just not doing anything right, and that everything is my fault. Like, if the baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not feeding her right, or if she's not sleeping, it's because I didn't establish a good routine. I just feel like I'm constantly messing everything up, and that I'm not good enough to be a mom. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Even when my husband tries to tell me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't shake the feeling that I'm failing somehow. And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. If the house is a mess, I feel like it's because I'm not managing my time well enough, or if I'm feeling tired, it's because I'm not taking care of myself. (shaking head) I just feel like I'm always falling short, and that I'm not living up to my own expectations. (tearfully) It's just really hard for me to be kind to myself and to give myself a break. I feel like I'm just not good enough, no matter what I do.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much? Is she too hot or too cold? I just can't seem to shake the feeling that something is going to go wrong, and that I'm not prepared for it. (bites lip) Even when my husband or my doctor tells me that everything is fine, I just can't help but worry. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if she chokes on something? What if she gets sick? What if I'm not doing enough to keep her safe? (takes a deep breath) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to get rid of. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I worry about my relationship with my husband, I worry about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and the house, I worry about my own health... (trails off, looking overwhelmed) It's just so much, and it feels like it's all the time. I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll just start thinking about all these things, and I won't be able to fall asleep because I'm so worried. (starts to tear up) It's just really hard to calm myself down and feel like everything is going to be okay.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, looking anxious) Yes, that's happened to me a few times. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (takes a deep breath) It's really scary, because it feels like it's coming out of nowhere. I'll be thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why am I feeling like this?" And then I'll start to worry that something's wrong with the baby, or that something's going to happen to me, and it just spirals out of control. (shakes head) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body just takes over and I feel like I'm in fight-or-flight mode, even though there's no reason for it.

(pauses, collecting thoughts) It's happened a few times when I'm alone with the baby, and that's when it's the scariest. I'll be thinking, "What if something happens to me? Who's going to take care of the baby?" And then I'll start to feel like I'm going to lose control or something. (looks down, embarrassed) It's just really hard to deal with, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this capable, confident mom, and instead I'm just feeling scared and overwhelmed all the time.

(looks up, tears in eyes) I just wish I could feel calm and peaceful, you know? I wish I could just enjoy this time with my baby without all this anxiety and fear. But it feels like it's always lurking there, just beneath the surface, waiting to pounce. (sighs, feeling helpless) I don't know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water, and that everything is just piling up on me. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to get enough sleep... it's just so much. And some days, it feels like it's all just too much for me to handle. (sighs) I'll be sitting there, feeling overwhelmed, and I'll just think, "How am I going to get everything done? How am I going to take care of this tiny human and still take care of myself?" And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and the baby will be crying, and I'll just feel like I'm at my breaking point.

(looks down, feeling frustrated) And it's not just the tasks themselves, it's the emotional weight of everything too. I feel like I'm responsible for this tiny person's entire well-being, and that's a huge burden to carry. Some days, it feels like I'm just shouldering all of this responsibility on my own, and it's hard to know how to ask for help or who to turn to. (pauses, collecting thoughts) I guess what I'm saying is that, yes, things have been getting on top of me. It's like, I'm just trying to survive each day, and I'm not really living. I'm just going through the motions, trying to get everything done, and it's exhausting.

(looks up, tears in eyes) I just wish I could feel like I'm on top of things, you know? I wish I could feel like I'm a capable, competent mom, and that I'm doing a good job. But most days, I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. (sighs, feeling defeated) It's hard to explain, but it's just this constant feeling of being overwhelmed, and not knowing how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding) Yes, that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. I mean, that's definitely part of it, but it's also because my mind just won't shut off. I'll be lying in bed, and I'll start thinking about all the things that are worrying me, like the baby's health, or my relationship with my husband, or just feeling like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom. And then I'll start to feel anxious and overwhelmed, and it's hard to calm down.

(sighs) Some nights, I'll be awake for hours, just lying there and thinking about everything that's bothering me. And even when I do finally fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm not really sleeping, I'm just existing. And it's hard, because I know that I need sleep to be a good mom, but it's just not happening.

(looks down, feeling frustrated) And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the emotional toll it's taking on me too. I feel like I'm just so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time, and it's hard to see a way out of it. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And it's not just sadness, it's hopelessness too. I'll think to myself, "Is this it? Is this just my life now? Am I always going to feel this way?"

(looks up, tears in eyes) I just wish I could feel happy again, you know? I wish I could feel like myself, like I did before I had the baby. But right now, it just feels like everything is too much for me, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just sad all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. It's not just feeling a little down, it's feeling completely overwhelmed and miserable. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start to feel this wave of sadness wash over me. And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a mom now and not a person anymore.

(sniffles) I'll be doing everyday tasks, like laundry or dishes, and I'll just start to feel so overwhelmed and sad. I'll think to myself, "Is this it? Is this my life now? Am I just going to be stuck in this rut forever?" And it's hard, because I know I'm supposed to be happy and grateful for this new baby, but it's just not how I'm feeling.

(looks down, feeling ashamed) Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start to feel so sad and overwhelmed that I'll start to cry. And it's not just a little cry, it's a full-on sob. I'll be sitting there, holding this tiny person who is completely dependent on me, and I'll just feel so lost and alone. And it's hard, because I don't know how to explain it to anyone. I don't know how to say, "Hey, I'm really struggling here. I'm not okay."

(looks up, tears streaming down face) I just wish someone would ask me how I'm really doing, you know? I wish someone would say, "Hey, are you okay? Really okay?" Because I'm not okay. I'm not okay at all. I'm sad, and I'm miserable, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start to feel this overwhelming sadness and I'll start to cry. It's not just a little cry, either. It's a full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath cry. And it's hard, because I don't always know what's triggering it. Sometimes it's just the exhaustion, or the feeling of being overwhelmed. Other times it's because I'm just feeling so sad and alone.

(sniffles) I've been trying to hide it from my husband, because I don't want him to worry. But it's hard, because I feel like I'm just falling apart. I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just start to cry. And it's not just when I'm alone, either. I've cried in front of my husband, in front of my family... it's just like, I don't have any control over it anymore.

(looks down, feeling embarrassed) I feel like I'm just so weak, you know? I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, and instead I'm just a mess. I'm crying all the time, and I don't know how to stop. It's like, I'll be sitting there, feeling fine, and then suddenly I'll just start to think about everything that's been going on, and I'll just start to cry. It's hard, because I feel like I'm just so emotional all the time, and I don't know how to regulate my feelings anymore.

(looks up, tears streaming down face) I just wish someone would tell me that it's okay, you know? That it's okay to feel this way, and that it's okay to not be okay. Because right now, I just feel like I'm drowning in all of these emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt

Further evaluation and potential referral for treatment are recommended to address these concerns and ensure the patient's safety and well-being.
